purpose: Teach: 車検/よき/よん/缶詰/立ち読み/度々/あした/嫌がらせ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の車、車検、自分で、整備していたな、ばあさん、覚えてる?今、思うと、若かったわね、私。
lines.en: When I was young, I used to maintain the car myself—inspections, repairs, everything. Do you remember that, dear? I was really young then, wasn't I.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Traces fingers through memory. Gentle pace, almost conversational with himself. Warm glance toward her at the end—not seeking reassurance, just reaching back.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。よき友、長く、付き合えてくれて、本当に、ありがたいわよね、あなた、お互いに、感謝、しないとね。
lines.en: Yes, I do. We've been lucky to have such a good friend for so long. We really should thank each other more, you know. We're lucky.
lines.style: Steady, affectionate tone. Not gushing—matter-of-fact about the gratitude, which makes it deeper. Soft emphasis on 「ありがたい」. A small, genuine smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、孫、よん歳の時、本当に、可愛かったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる、写真、いっぱい、撮ったよね?
lines.en: When the grandkid was four years old, they were so adorable. You remember that, don't you? We took so many photos back then.
lines.style: Soft brightness surfaces. The memory catches him. Pace slows on the image of the child. Seeking her confirmation gently, not as a question but as an invitation to share the moment again.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 非常用の缶詰、地震に備えて、ストックしておきましょうね、あなた、お互いに、年だしね、慎重にね。
lines.en: We should stock up on emergency supplies—canned goods, that sort of thing. For earthquakes, you know. We're getting older, so we need to be careful about these things.
lines.style: Practical, matter-of-fact. Not fearful—steady and grounded. A light touch of gentle firmness, like someone who's thought this through and wants to make sure. Clear, unhurried.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、立ち読み、本屋で、よく、したな、ばあさん、お金、なかったから、本、読みたかったよ。
lines.en: When I was young, I used to browse in the bookstore a lot—just standing there reading for free. We didn't have much money, but I really wanted to read those books.
lines.style: Wistful again, but with a thread of quiet humor at his own younger self. No complaint—just remembering the hunger. Pace is steady, slightly slower on the admission about money.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 息子、度々、訪ねてくれるって、本当に、嬉しいわよね、あなた、私たち、孫にも、会えて、幸せよ。
lines.en: It's wonderful that our son visits so often. And to think we get to see the grandkids too—we're truly blessed. We've been so lucky.
lines.style: Warm, genuine contentment. Not effusive—this is someone stating a fact that moves her quietly. Slight lift on the gratitude. Simple, direct, anchored.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: あした、お祭り、町内会、参加しよう、ばあさん、お互いに、足が、健康なうちにね、お互い、楽しまないと。
lines.en: Tomorrow the neighborhood festival is on. Why don't we go, dear? While our legs are still healthy enough, we should enjoy these things together.
lines.style: A gentle suggestion, almost coaxing. Not commanding—offering. Light and hopeful underneath. Slight pause before 「楽しまないと」, as if he's saying: we won't have forever, so let's.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔、嫌がらせ、めいた、いたずら、ご近所で、あったわね、あなた、覚えてる?今、思うと、軽くて、笑えるわよね。
lines.en: You know, there used to be some pretty annoying pranks going on in the neighborhood back then. Do you remember? But looking back on it now, it's kind of funny—such silly stuff.
lines.style: Dry affection. A small chuckle in the voice. She's inviting him to laugh at the past with her. Easy, conspiratorial tone—two people who survived it together and can see the humor now.
